immediateBlocker.fix: FILE handmade/src/sb_router.h FN sb_af38_descriptor_response (stock CODE_BANK1::af38). The device TXes a wrong connect-descriptor response, so the host posts C0 (not F3) into 0x081A and the a7de latch 0x0819.0 = (0x077A.0 && 0x081A.0) fails (0x077A=F3 from eaac has bit0=1; host's C0 has bit0=0). TWO concrete stock divergences cause it: (1) BRANCH DIRECTION IS INVERTED. Stock af8b-af8f: `MOV A,DAT_52; JNZ af92; LJMP b024` => DAT_52!=0 takes the af92 block (sets 0x0754=1, the RX-plane->0x0800 work-buffer copy), DAT_52==0 takes the b024 block (sets 0x0754=DAT_51, the work-buffer->0x2900 TX copy). Handmade has it backwards: it runs `if(dat52==0){0x0754=1; RX->work}else{0x0754=dat51; work->TX}`. SWAP the two arms so dat52!=0 => 0x0754=1 + RX->work, dat52==0 => 0x0754=dat51 + work->TX. (2) BOTH ARMS ARE GATED in stock; handmade copies unconditionally with no fail-response. Transcribe the gate. Resolved helper semantics: 99b5(R7) sets DAT_4f = R7-5 (R7 = SB[0x0D|0x0E]&0x7f, the per-port TX status read at afad-afb8/b02a-b03f, port0=SB[0x0D] R2=0x28 else SB[0x0E]) and returns CY=(DAT_50<0x12); 976e(A)=XDATA[0x0600+A] read with A=DAT_50-0xe i.e. the per-type width LUT PR(0x06F2+(DAT_50-0xe)). af92/BRANCH-A gate (afb9-afdf): PASS only if (DAT_50<0x12) AND (PR(0x06F2+(DAT_50-0xe))!=0) AND (DAT_51==DAT_4f i.e DAT_51==status-5) AND (CODE[0x0700+(DAT_50+5)]!=0 via movc) AND (DAT_51 <= LUTwidth); on FAIL jump afe1: call 9988() then SBTX[1]=1 (r3_write 1 to 0x2901) and FALL THROUGH to b096 WITHOUT the copy. b024/BRANCH-B gate (b040-b054): PASS only if (DAT_50<0x12) AND (PR(0x06F2+(DAT_50-0xe))!=0) AND (DAT_4f==0 i.e. status==5); on FAIL jump b056: 9988() + 0x0754=0 + skip copy. On PASS, b060-b072 CLAMPS 0x0754 to the 976e LUT width before the copy. Then the SHARED b096 tail (status byte = (0x0754+8)|(SB[0x0C]&0x80) to SB[0x0D|0x0E], SB[0x15]=0x0753, d5da(0) trigger) runs in ALL cases. Implement: read r7status=SB[port0?0x0D:0x0E]&0x7f; dat4f=r7status-5; gate as above per-branch; on fail do { (void)SBTX_RD(1); SBTX_WR(1,1); 0x0754=(branchB?0)(branchA leaves 0x0754=1 already); } and SKIP the copy; on pass clamp 0x0754 to PR(0x06F2+(dat50-0xe)) then copy. REMOVE the sb_af38_force_budget all-zero forced-TX probe entirely (it TXes garbage on the live path). Also: af38's diag label '81A= af38 dest' is FALSE (af38 never writes 0x081A); drop/relabel.

verify.reasoning:
I independently verified the immediateBlocker (af38) and the top 5 orderedFixes against the raw stock ghidra disassembly/decompile. The core claims hold up; the plan is NOT refuted. Details below.

== immediateBlocker / Order 1 (af38 branch inversion + gate) — CONFIRMED REAL ==
Raw af38 disasm (af8b-af8f): `MOV A,0x52; JNZ af92; LJMP b024`. So DAT_52!=0 -> af92, DAT_52==0 -> b024. I traced both bodies via the plane helpers (9a38 loads the SRC plane tuple 0x755 = 0x2a00/0x2b00; 96a7 reads work-buffer XDATA[0x0800+x]; 99e7 returns plane 0x29 = TX 0x2900). Result: af92 (DAT_52!=0) sets 0x0754=1 and copies SRC/RX-plane(0x2a00)->work[0x0800+0x53+i] (loop b008 reads SRC, b00c-b014 writes work). b024 (DAT_52==0) sets 0x0754=DAT_51 and copies work[0x0800+..]->TX-plane(0x2900+2+i) (b081 96a7 reads work, b08b 99e7 -> 0be6 writes 0x29 plane). The HANDMADE (sb_router.h lines 210-235) assigns af92's body to its `dat52==0` arm and b024's body to its `dat52!=0` arm — i.e. the two arms are SWAPPED relative to stock. The branch-inversion claim is genuinely real, not a hand-reasoned guess.
The 3-condition gate is also real: stock gates BOTH arms (afb9 99b5/afbc JNC afe1; afc6 JZ; afca CJNE 0x51,0x4f; afd9 JZ; afdf JC for branch-A; b040/b04d/b054 for branch-B) and on FAIL calls 9988() + writes SBTX[1]=1 (branch A, afe1-afe7) or 9988()+0x0754=0 (branch B, b056-b05d), then falls through to the SHARED b096 tail WITHOUT the copy. Handmade copies UNCONDITIONALLY with no gate and no fail-response. 99b5 verified: sets DAT_4f=R7-5, returns CY=(DAT_50<0x12). 976e verified: returns XDATA[0x0600+param]. So the gate transcription in the fix is accurate.

== Order 2 (d5da 'byte-exact, keep') — PARTIALLY REFUTED (overstated) ==
Stock d5da (decompiled) has a TRAILING `if(0x0AAC==0){ if(SB[0x0C]>6) zero TX-plane 0x29xx from 0..(SB[0x0C]-6) }` loop that the handmade d5da reproduction (sb_router.h lines 253-260) OMITS entirely. Also the handmade uses `phy_cc10_cmd(1,0,0x0B)` where stock calls e80a with R7=1 (subcmd 1) — cc12/cc13=0x0B is unverified against the 051b call site. The audit labels order-2 'verified byte-exact'; that is an overstatement. Likely not load-bearing for the 0x081A latch (the trailing loop only clears TX-plane tail), but the 'byte-exact' claim is false.

== Order 3 (b7a4 0x081A.5 clear-back) — plausible, not independently re-verified here (in sb.h, outside my decompile budget); accept as MED, treat as unverified per default-skeptic.

== Order 4 (eaac faithful) — CONFIRMED. Stock eaac: 0x0775=1; loop i=0..0x40 copies SBP2[base+i]->XDATA 0x0777+i (dest CONCAT11(6,0x77+i)); 97ef() = CCD9=4 then 2. Handmade matches byte-for-byte. Keep.

== Order 5/6 (cd3f dispatch + edd9 tail) — CONFIRMED divergence ==
Stock cd3f head = `LCALL edd9` (cd3f), and the 3-way dispatch (ebb5 / eaac / af38) matches handmade's structure. BUT stock edd9 (edd9-edf4) runs `eb62(0,3); 98ec(0,3)` INSIDE the page1-0x0109.0 gate (edea-edf1), which handmade's sb_edd9_receive_ack DROPS (admitted in comment). The edd9 gate itself is correctly transcribed: 9779(9) reads page1 0x0109, `JNB ACC.0` = `if(P1[0x0109]&1)` — handmade's gate is right; only the eb62+98ec tail is missing. Order 6 is real.
Order 7 (sb_chan_prelude wrong-register stub) ALSO CONFIRMED: c3b2 head is LCALL edd9; handmade calls sb_chan_prelude = (void)SB_RD(0x09), the wrong register. Real bug.

== Order 8 (dea1) — CONFIRMED, multiple real divergences ==
Stock dea1 (dea1-defe) has NO `if(0x06EC)return` early-return, NO CC11 poll/W1C, NO IE_EX1 mask, NO ec51 inline. It runs 989b/gate, the SB[0x00]/[0x04]/[0x01]/P1[0x0100] RMW block, e80a via 051b (R7=2 -> subcmd=2,cc12=0,cc13=0x15), sets 0x06EC=1, then `LJMP db7a`. Handmade adds ALL of: the 0x06EC early-return (line 491), an invented CC11 poll+W1C (519-520), the IE_EX1 mask (555), 8a89-pending (547), and inlines ec51+98ec-snapshot (537-545). All confirmed hand-reasoned. The dea1 e80a arg (2,0,0x15) IS faithful.

== Order 10 (98ec stores wrong cells) — CONFIRMED BLOCKER ==
Stock 98ec(p1,p2): 0x0758=0x10; ee57(); 0x0768=R6(=p1); 0x0769=R7(=p2). db7a/edd9 both call 98ec(0,3). Handmade inlines 0x0768=CCE4, 0x0769=CCE5 (dea1 lines 544-545) — stores HW regs instead of the (0,3) params. Genuine divergence; the 'lane-width snapshot' label is wrong (98ec just stores its two args).

== Order 9 (db7a tail) — CONFIRMED. Stock db7a ends with eb62(0,3)+98ec(0,3); handmade omits these in sb_db7a_route_arm (admitted) and instead inlines them in dea1. The 0x07B9!=0 else-branch helpers (98de/984d/98e4/975e) are reproduced as masked-self no-ops in handmade — real fidelity gap, lower priority (0x07B9==0 is the live path).

NET: the immediateBlocker and orders 4-10 are correctly diagnosed and the fixes are byte-faithful (modulo the minor 9988/d5da approximations noted). I do not refute the plan. I flag the order-2 'byte-exact' overstatement and a couple of fix-text approximations as criticalIssues, and note missed jank items.
criticalIssues: Order 2 is mis-labeled 'verified byte-exact': stock d5da has a TRAILING `if(0x0AAC==0){if(SB[0x0C]>6) zero TX-plane 0x29xx[0..SB[0x0C]-6]}` clear loop (decompile of CODE_BANK1::d5da) that the handmade d5da reproduction (sb_router.h lines 253-260) omits entirely. Also handmade's `phy_cc10_cmd(1,0,0x0B)` vs stock e80a(subcmd=1) leaves cc12/cc13=0x0B unverified against the 051b call site. The 'keep, no structural change' verdict should be downgraded to 'verify the trailing TX-clear loop is non-load-bearing and confirm the e80a args'.

Order 1 fix-text approximates the af38 FAIL-path helper 9988 as `(void)SBTX_RD(1)`. Stock 9988 actually does `SBTX[1] = SBTX[1] & 0x80` (read-modify-WRITE clearing bits0-6 of 0x2901), not a discarded read. Branch-A fail then does INC R1 + SBTX[1]=1; branch-B fail does 0x0754=0. Transcribe 9988 as the &0x80 RMW, not a no-op read, to stay byte-faithful.

Order 1 omits that the SHARED b096 tail begins with `9695()` = a discarded read of SB[0x0C] (r3_read 0x280c) BEFORE building the status byte. The status byte high bit comes from THAT 9695 read (b099 ANL #0x80), i.e. (SB[0x0C]&0x80) is the result of 9695's read of 0x280c, which the handmade approximates as SB_RD(0x0C). This is consistent but the fix text should keep the 9695 read ordering since it shares the SB accessor state.

The immediateBlocker's premise that the af38 force_budget probe 'TXes garbage on the live path' is overstated: main.c line 687 seeds sb_af38_force_budget=0, so the probe is dead code on the live path (gated `if(sb_af38_force_budget && ...)`). Removing it is correct hygiene but it is NOT actively corrupting the connect; the justification should be 'dead probe, remove for clarity' not 'TXes garbage live'.
missedIssues: sb_connect_present_poll (sb_router.h lines 383-386) contains a hand-reasoned 'spec-sanctioned equivalent' that pokes ebb5's effect from the super-loop whenever 0x06EC==1 (`if(PR(0x06EC)){PR(0x0752)=SB_RD(0x18); sb_set_connect_present_ebb5();}`). This is exactly the 'documented-equivalent / spec-sanctioned equivalent' jank the user wants removed, and the stock cd3f reaches ebb5 ONLY via its real dispatch gate ((0x752&0x60)==0x60). Order 5 says 'keep cd3f faithful' but does NOT call for removing this super-loop ebb5 short-circuit. It should be removed alongside the af38 probe.

edd9 double-arm risk: once order 6 restores eb62(0,3)+98ec(0,3) inside sb_edd9_receive_ack AND order 8/9 also place the eb62+98ec tail in dea1/db7a, the route-query sub-FSM (0x06ED=3, 0x0758=0x10) could be armed twice per connect edge (cd3f calls edd9 first, then dea1->db7a calls it again). Stock has THREE distinct 98ec callers (edd9, db7a, dea1->db7a) but they run at different FSM phases; the plan should specify the ordering so the super-loop's per-iteration cd3f doesn't repeatedly reset 0x0758=0x10 mid-route-query.

Order 10 should also note db7a/edd9 call 98ec(0,3) i.e. p1=0, p2=3 -> 0x0768=0, 0x0769=3 (NOT a snapshot of anything). The plan says 'db7a calls 98ec(0,3)' but the eed9 path and the handmade's claim that 0x0768/0x0769 is a 'lane-width snapshot b0b4 diffs' is the actual root mislabel — b0b4's width gate reads 0x0768/0x0769 expecting 0/3 sentinels, so storing CCE4/CCE5 there actively poisons b0b4. Confirm b0b4's consumer reads 0/3, not a width, before assuming the fix restores correct behavior.

The handmade dea1 reproduction calls e80a via a bounded CC11 poll that is INVENTED (order 8 flags removing it), but stock's 051b/e80a (the real phy_cmd_and_wait) has its OWN internal wait. If e80a's handmade implementation (boot_phy.h, not audited in top-5) does NOT actually wait, removing the dea1 CC11 poll could regress timing. The plan should verify boot_phy.h's phy_cc10_cmd(2,0,0x15) blocks on the PHY-cmd-done event before deleting the dea1 poll, otherwise order 8 trades one hack for a race.
